body.name: primitive Gaussian proximal family
body.construction: For \(\theta=(\mu,f,b,x,y,\zeta,r,t_1,t_2)\in\Theta_{\mathcal G}^{\mathrm{leg}}\) and \(d\in\mathbb R\), set \(B=\mu^2+f\), \(R=t_1+B+x\), \(\eta=B/R\), \(K=\mu/B\), \(c_1=t_1^{-1/2}\), \(t_{2,n}=t_2-(R^2/B^2)d/\sqrt n\), and \(c_{2,n}=t_{2,n}^{-1/2}\). Generate independent Gaussian coordinates \(F_t\sim N(\mu,f)\), \(e_{0t}\sim N(0,b)\), \(e_{1t}\sim N(0,x)\), \(e_{2t}\sim N(0,y)\), and \(\xi_t\sim N(0,\zeta)\); put \(Y_t(0)=F_t+e_{0t}\), \(\Delta_t=\tau+\xi_t\), \(W_{1t}=c_1(F_t+e_{1t})\), and \(W_{2t}=c_{2,n}(F_t+e_{2t})\), with the two roles exchanging donor and proxy positions. The legal tied manifold has \(t_2=t_1+x-y>0\); along the local calibration, \(t_{2,n}>0\) eventually, both bridge matrices equal \(c_1c_{2,n}B\), the bridge coefficients are \(1/c_1\) and \(1/c_{2,n}\), and \(\sqrt n(L_1-L_2)=d+O(n^{-1/2})\). At the tied limit, \(\sigma_D^2=4\eta^2\{(1-\eta)^2B+b\}(x+y)+2\eta^4(x^2+y^2)\), \(c_{D1}=\operatorname{Cov}(D,A_1)=-2\eta K\{(1-\eta)Bx+by\}\), \(c_{D2}=\operatorname{Cov}(D,A_2)=2\eta K\{(1-\eta)By+bx\}\), \(V_1=K^2(B+y)(b+x)+r(b+x+\zeta)\), and \(V_2=K^2(B+x)(b+y)+r(b+y+\zeta)\). Hence the continuous map is \(\Gamma(\theta,d)=(-d/\sigma_D,c_{D1}/\sqrt{\sigma_D^2V_1},c_{D2}/\sqrt{\sigma_D^2V_2},V_1,V_2)\). The family \(\mathcal G\) is the collection of these local Gaussian arrays.
